Массовый импорт лежит в глоссарии уровне:
The bulk import sits in the glossary at the “hint” level: it goes into the prompt marked “not checked, some of it is wrong” and with explicit permission to ignore it. Purging it has NO effect at all on a translation that is already done — divergences and repairs are counted only from entries at the “verified” level.

One thing changes: what the model will use on the NEXT translation. Along with the rubbish, raw material goes too: a hint rises to verified when several independent clean segments agree on one translation.

Entries a human has touched (approving a candidate, editing by hand, undoing a demotion) are never purged — the report says how many there are. Everything purged goes as a file into data/backups and comes back with a rollback.

A pair gets into the glossary by itself only if: the term has exactly one translation option in the queue; the same pair came from several independent segments OR a human confirmed the segment; the donor segments passed the back-check and the terminology check cleanly; the pair does not argue with a verified entry.

By default the entry goes in at the “hint” level — the model may ignore it. It becomes verified (“use these exact translations”) from a human or from three independent clean segments, and in medicine, pharmacy and law — only from a human.

The rules do not depend on the language or the subject: what counts is the agreement of sources and the scores of other runs, not the opinion of the model that did the translation.

Приказная запись глоссария заставляет мо:
A verified glossary entry makes the model write exactly this translation and serves as grounds for a repair. No other check asks whether it is THE SAME concept: the corpus only confirms that the string exists in the language, the term check that the term is real, the agreement of segments that the model repeats itself. “Anizakidoz → Anisakis” (a disease against a parasite genus) passes all of them.

A finding is DEMOTED to a hint rather than deleted: the translation stays where it is, the entry stays visible, but it stops commanding the model and driving repairs.

Entries carrying the trace of a human decision (approving a candidate, editing by hand) are never demoted — they are only marked. The machine may revise its own assumption, but not somebody else’s decision.
